Before the Age of Fire was the Age of Ancients. It was a time in which the world was colorless and shrouded by fog. The land consisted of gray crags, archtrees and Everlasting Dragons, who were the rulers of the world. Humans and other creatures had yet to make an impression upon the world.

title: Age of Ancients

 lore : In the Age of Ancients the world was undistinguished and covered in fog: a land of gray rocks, great trees and everlasting dragons; everything was the same and time didn't exist.But at some point the First Flame appeared and brought "disparity" into the world, allowing the existence of everything and its opposite: heat and cold, life and death, light and dark.

It was during this time that the Lord Souls were found near the Flame. The three Lords who found them (Nito, Gwyn and the Witch of Izalith) formed a coalition and used the power of their newly discovered souls to challenge the Dragons, starting a very long and destructive war. However, there was a fourth Lord Soul, the Dark Soul, which was found by the Furtive Pygmy. The only known act via this Lord was the fragmentation of their soul becoming the birth of Humanity, who would fight side by side with the Lords.

The Age of Fire first began after Gwyn and the other Lords defeated the Everlasting Dragons which ended the Age of Ancients. The Age of Fire was unnaturally prolonged when Gwyn sacrificed himself to kindle the First Flame.

When the Chosen Undead talks to Kingseeker Frampt, he will tell them that they are destined to succeed Gwyn. Should the player choose to kindle the First Flame upon the defeat of Gwyn, they will sacrifice themselves as Gwyn did, thus delaying the Age of Dark once more.

Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

Calling it "futile" is a euphemism: the unnatural prolonging of the First Flame's lifespan came with disastrous, if not, downright catastrophical proportions: when the Lords of Cinder started to resurrect, somehow, portions of their countries and homelands were, literally, "teleported" to Lothric, changing the landscape in unpredictable ways.

By the time *Dark Souls 3* takes place, the damage caused to the world by the unnatural prolonging of the Age of Fire seems to be irreversible.

As the games progresses, the sun itself starts to change, until it eerily resembles the Darksign itself.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
As the games progresses, the sun itself starts to change, until it eerily resembles the Darksign itself.

At the end of the game, after defeating the Soul of Cinder, the Ashen One, in case they chose to link the First Flame, is covered from head to toe in a soft-looking fire, unlike the flaming inferno of the first game. The implications are clear: The First Flame itself now is so weak that it cannot be kindled anymore.

The First Flame, as the Age of Fire, is beyond saving.

In *The Ringed City*, it is implied that the unnatural prolonging of the Age of Fire has caused irrepairable damage to the world, as is shown after Filianore's awakening: the fertile lands seen when the Ashen One arrived in the city are replaced by a seemingly unending, as-far-the-eye-can-see's barren wasteland of unknown nature.

title: First Flame
snippet: But then, somewhere in the hollows deep underground, a great and primordial fire that would come to be known as the First Flame burst into being. In doing so, it brought disparities into the world for the first time, such as heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. Soon, humanoid creatures emerged from the darkness surrounding the First Flame, attracted by the fire. These creatures found sources of power called souls near the Flame, and took on the diverse powers the souls gave them. With the strength of four particularly powerful souls, four figures were born: Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith, Gwyn, the Lord of Sunlight, and the Furtive Pygmy. Using their newfound power, these Lords and their forces overthrew the ancient dragons, ushering in the Age of Fire.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Although the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods lasted for centuries, at some point the First Flame began to fade. Gwyn understood that if the Flame went out, the Age of Fire would be succeeded by an Age of Dark, a new order of humans led by a Dark Lord. Fearful of this outcome, the god made a drastic decision: In order to maintain the order of Gods, he would sacrifice himself to link the dying Flame and prolong its life. He trusted none but himself to carry out the sacrifice involved; he thus divided the power of his Lord Soul among the members of his clan and handed down the power of the sun to his children, leaving his firstborn son to inherit his titles. Gwyn also tasked his sons and Frampt with shepherding the humans into following his example, linking the Flame generation after generation, to uphold his Age of Fire, each of them becoming Lords through the process.

 lore : The Age of Dark begins when the First Flame fades completely, thus ending the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods that gained their power from it.
Since the Flame continues to burn until it goes out naturally, the Dark Age should have arrived, as naturally, when it had exhausted its fuel.

Despite the Age of Dark being a ubiquitous concept throughout the *Dark Souls* series, it is never the "current" state of the world in any of the existing games. Each of the *Dark Souls* games takes place during a late point in the Age of Fire, a point which could theoretically lead to the beginning of the Age of Dark, but which does not do so during the normal course of gameplay, with one possible exception.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: What exactly the term "Age of Dark" implies is never made explicitly clear in the games, however it is stated in the canonical *Dark Souls Trilogy Compendium* to be a time when the Light fades, a Dark Lord is heralded, and humanity dominates the world. When the protagonists are given information about the Age of Dark, it typically comes from the mouths of potentially unreliable narrators, of whom Kaathe and his counterpart, Kingseeker Frampt, are examples. Kaathe asserts that the Age of Dark is "the age of men," presumably meaning the Age of those possessing Humanity in contrast to the Age of the Gods, and also declares that Gwyn "resisted the course of nature" when he linked the Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire.

title: First Flame
snippet:
Aware that time was quickly running out for his kingdom, Gwyn and a detachment of his knights entered the Kiln of the First Flame. The knights stood guard as Gwyn sacrificed himself to the waning Flame at the Kiln's centre. This immediately reinvigorated the First Flame, creating a firestorm that turned the Kiln to ash, and incinerated all of Gwyn's knights, creating the Black Knights and dooming them to wander the lands as disembodied spirits forever after.

Gwyn's sacrifice succeeded in perpetuating the Age of Fire for a time, but *Dark Souls* takes place at least 1000 years later, and the Flame is quickly fading once again. Soon, only Dark will remain.

title: Dark Lord
snippet: The interpretation of the Dark Lord's role in founding a new world order seems to have varied over time. The "Dark Lord" ending of *Dark Souls I* entails abandoning the First Flame to die out and beginning a new age from naught; the "Usurpation of Fire" ending of *Dark Souls III* however is somewhat different. Many millennia past the time of the Chosen Undead, the Sable Church of Londor, founded by three sisters who were disciples of Kaathe, are searching for a worthy Lord of Men. If the Ashen One cooperates with Yuria, a sister of the Sable Church, they are asked to "usurp the Flame", to "wrest it from its mantle". title: Lore
snippet: The Age of Fire began prosperous and rich, but soon the fires started to go out again and with them the power of the Lords. In an effort to prolong Age of Fire, the Witch of Izalith tried to recreate the First Flame, but the experiment failed and a flame called "The Flame of Chaos" is created instead, which transformed her into the Bed of Chaos and many creatures into the demons that roam Lordran. Her children are transformed as well, with her son becoming a flame demon called Ceaseless Discharge and her daughter Quelaag and her sister partially into spiders. Her followers stay loyal to her, however, and become known as the "Witches of Chaos". Only her daughter, Quelana, escaped the fire and becomes the mother of pyromancy. This being said, Mother Izalith did eventually *succeed* in stabilizing the Chaos Flame with 2 of her sisters.

As the First Flame began to fade, the Darksign's power consequently weakened and, as it was no longer able to adequately contain the Dark Soul, humans returned to being immortal, coming back to life with each death, and becoming known as Undead. title: Primordial Serpents
snippet: Even eons past the first linking of the Flame, Kaathe didn't stop trying to bring the Age of Dark. The serpent took into his service what would become the three sisters at the helm of the Sable Church of Londor: Liliane, Yuria and Elfriede. He then directed their efforts to create a realm inhabited by Hollows that could offer salvation to them. Kaathe taught them his dark powers, and Londor carried out experiments aimed at understanding the Darksign and the Dark Soul under his watch. Their goal evolved into usurping the First Flame, tearing it from its Kiln and ensuring that it could be wielded to finally create a new Age of Man. To this end, the Sable Church awaited the arrival of a chosen Unkindled, preparing to assist and guide them to ensure that they succeeded in their goal. However, before he could see his dream of an Age of Dark realized, Kaathe died of unknown causes, leaving the three sisters to continue to lead Londor and await the future Dark Lord.

title: First sin
snippet: Similarly, after the Lords were successful in defeating the Ancient Dragons, Gwyn used his Soul to build a civilization above-ground, for humans to worship the gods in; allowing the Furtive Pygmy's descendants to come out of their abyssal caverns and live in the sunlight. The gods built a city of castles above this world from which to rule, and effectively made ingress impossible without great strength. However, in the stead of humanity taking the plunge into sin, it is Anor Londo, following the lead of its king. Thus - perhaps symbolic of this inversion - humankind becomes damned to eternal life instead of the persistent death of reality; and the gods of *Dark Souls* become ineffectual rulers, where systems similarly devolve into chaos in real life, but as designated by Providence.

title: Lothric
snippet: In the beginning, the first Fire Keeper had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a barren plane of endless darkness. Acting to ward off an Age of Dark, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition of Courland, rose to the challenge of becoming a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Despite his feeble appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Lord, something for which he himself expresses remorse, asking to be forgiven. Ludleth was exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric to ensure that the Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes, as well as all future maidens, to prevent them from observing a future without the Flame. The original eyes were sealed away in an enigmatic instance of Firelink Shrine, where the First Flame had all but gone out.

title: Dark Lord

 lore : **This section of the lore lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations**

The Dark Lords are beings who were meant to become Lords of Cinder, but refused to link the First Flame and extend the Age of Fire, with the specific intent of bringing forth the Age of Dark (also referred to as an "Age of Man"). Dark Lords, while powerful enough to overcome the trials involved in linking the Flame, apparently don't have to inherit a primordial force (such as the First Flame) in order to be deemed worthy of their title. For instance, if the Chosen Undead chooses to become a Dark Lord, abandoning the power of the First Flame, several primordial serpents will nevertheless bow before their new Lord (including both Kaathe and Frampt), even as the Chosen Undead lacks the extraordinary power granted by the Flame.

title: Liliane
snippet: Liliane is a founding mentor of the Sable Church, and the youngest sister to Elfriede and Yuria. The three sisters at one point entered into the service of the Primordial Serpent Kaathe, becoming his maidens. The Primordial Serpent taught them his art of the Dark Hand, which could sap the essence of its victims. The sisters pursued Kaathe's goal of ending the Age of Fire founded by the gods and ushering the Age of Dark, and searched for a Dark Lord whom they would empower to usurp the First Flame and use its powers to lead humans into a new age. To this end, the three sisters used their battle prowess to establish the Sable Church, an organization that claimed to offer salvation to Hollows. The Church became a haven for those with unsavory or blurry pasts, along with other rejects of the Age of Fire. title: The Deep
snippet:
It is unclear what would have become of Aldrich at the end of the Age of Fire. While the champion of the Deep has already been defeated when the Ashen One visits the Ringed City or the Dreg Heap, it seems that his visions of an incoming Age of Deep Sea were close to coming to pass, with the remnants of the world of Man bustling with the sunken, stagnated dregs of humanity, the malformed legacy of the Dark Soul which had been suppressed by the Darksign for millennia.

According to the Primordial Serpent Kaathe, the gods were intimidated by this unexplored potential of the Dark Soul. They had briefly glimpsed at the smidgen of life emanated from the primordial human knights, and feared the eventual overthrow of Anor Londo and its Age of Fire. Therefore, a complex and ingenious apparatus was set in motion with the goal to mould humanity into a subservient, weak people that would not only serve the Age of Fire, but also refused to relinquish it to make way for the Age of Dark.

By choosing this ending, the Age of Fire is relinquished and Darkstalker Kaathe's goal of starting the Age of Dark is fulfilled.

title: Archtree
snippet:
Archtree -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : The Archtrees were entities that existed in the Age of Ancients, alongside the Archdragons. In this state, before the First Flame brought any form of life and diversity, the world was undistinguished and consequently everything was made of ash-colored rocks. Like dragons, archtrees were also made of stone and were half-living, half-mineral and simply existed without any changes. They covered the surface of the world, their roots kilometers deep with trunks reaching the sky. The rock wood of the archtrees was immensely capable of resisting magic.

title: Gertrude
snippet: Whatever the Angels communicated to Gertrude might have been the announcement of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of the Age of Dark, justifying the Kingdom's violent reaction. Given that Lothric culture essentially evolved around Firelinking, the Three Pillars had a stake in denouncing the revelations of the Angels who traced their roots to Londor, a realm devoted to bringing about an Age of Dark. Furthermore, the apparent ability of the Angel's miracle being able to manifest "light", counterintuitive to the Angels' somber origins, could have suggested that a world without flame would not be as "dark" as the Three Pillars would have Lothric believe.

title: Lords
snippet:
In his fear of the Age of Dark, he sacrificed himself to the First Flame, prolonging the Age of Fire and becoming Lord of Cinder. This act rendered Gwyn Hollow.

At some point, his firstborn son tamed a stormdrake, and allied with the dragon descendants. For this treachery, he was stripped of his godhood and banished (albeit, not by Gwyn), expunged from all records of history.

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet:
Witch of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : The **Witch of Izalith** or simply **Izalith** (イザリス) is a mentioned character in *Dark Souls*. She is also mentioned in *Dark Souls II*, although by that time her name is lost to history and only her nickname of "mother of pyromancy" remains.

A legendary fire sorcerer who found one of the four Lord Souls, she helped bring an end to the Age of Ancients and the rule of the dragons to establish the Age of Fire, and established an underground civilization named after her. She had many daughters, nicknamed the "Daughters of Chaos", which included Quelaag, Quelana and "The Fair Lady", as well as a son. By the time of the game's events, her magical experiments backfired, fusing her soul and two of her daughters' into a new horrible being, the Bed of Chaos. Although the Bed was eventually slain by the Chosen Undead and its soul fed to the Lordvessel, fragments of the Witch's soul survived.

title: Humans
snippet:
Kaathe also manipulated the inhabitants of New Londo, where he enticed the Four Kings with the art of Lifedrain, which ancient Humans used to steal Humanity from others. The Kings too were corrupted, and New Londo was flooded —presumably by the Gods— to contain the Abyss that generated there. But despite these failures, Kaathe kept searching for a human who could become the Dark Lord, and usher in the Age of Man.

At the close of the Age of Gods, Gwyn realized that the power of the Dark Soul would wax to its utmost maximum, while the power of the other Lord Souls would fade. Fearing that the world would be ruled by the Humans, Gwyn cast himself into the First Flame, artificially extending the Age of Fire for another thousand years. At Gwyn's command, The Gods shepherded the Human race afterwards.

title: Ludleth of Courland
snippet:
Ludleth of Courland -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Ludleth comes from Courland, a land known for its "transposition arts", the process of extracting and coalescing the essence of a soul and in doing so transferring its true power to the user. This art was able to grant powers once thought unattainable, but one that also left a foul stain upon Courland's honor. Ludleth himself mastered the art of transposition and offered his services away from home, given the right tools.

At a certain point the First Flame began to fade again and the first Fire Keeper of Lothric had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark. To repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper, Ludleth "willed himself" to become a Lord of Cinder. Defying his frail appearance, Ludleth somehow mustered the strength necessary to become a Champion.

title: Sister Friede
snippet: lore : Elfriede is the eldest sister of Yuria and Liliane. The three sisters at one point entered into the service of the Primordial Serpent Kaathe, becoming his maidens. The Primordial Serpent taught them his art of the Dark Hand, which could sap the essence of its victims. The sisters pursued Kaathe's goal of ending the Age of Fire founded by the gods and ushering the Age of Dark, and searched for a Dark Lord who could usurp the First Flame and use its powers to lead the humans into a new age. To this end, the three sisters used their battle prowess to establish the Sable Church, an organization that claimed to offer salvation to Hollows. Elfriede, the eldest sister, became its leader. The Church became a haven for those with unsavory or blurry pasts, along with other rejects of the Age of Fire. An increasing number of Undead and Hollows flocked to the Church, forming a society of wretchedly aged, deceitful, deeply detested Hollows. Their realm would be known as Londor, where

title: Darksign
snippet:
Centuries after this abuse, the First Flame started to naturally fade out, and the Darksign, which used the power of the Flame to contain the Dark Soul, weakened too, leading humans to come back to life as Undead, but also cursing them to eventually become Hollows, as the Darksign would consume their Humanity still forced on their bodies.
Thus, Gwyn sacrificed himself to rekindle the First Flame and forcibly postpone the end of the Age of Fire. Now with a martyr figure to use as powerful propaganda, the Undead Prophecy was spread throughout Lordran to encourage all who bear the Darksign to come to Lordran and claim powerful souls, making them worthy of filling the Lordvessel and succeed Lord Gwyn, rekindling the dying flame and prolonging the Age of Fire. The Chosen Undead would find themselves nearly hollow for several centuries after the rekindling of the First Flame, bearing the cursed mark of the Darksign, the greatest sin against humanity.

title: Chosen Undead
snippet:
Chosen Undead -  Dark Souls - character - epilogue 
 epilogue : After offering the necessary Lord Souls, the doors to the Kiln of the First Flame are opened to the Chosen Undead. Gwyn, now reduced to a Lord of Cinder, breathes his last breath in the final confrontation with the Chosen Undead. It is here that the Chosen Undead may make their decision of either linking the flame or walking away from it. Depending on which course of action is taken, one of the two possible endings will be unlocked. Whether the player has aligned themselves with Kaathe or Frampt will not affect the ending of the game.

***Link the Fire:** This ending is unlocked if the player rekindles the First Flame. The Chosen Undead offers themselves as kindling to the fire. Sacrificing all of their souls, the Chosen Undead is consumed by the flames and the Age of Fire is extended, as life is breathed into the First Flame once more.

title: Ending

Ending -  Dark Souls - mechanic - to_link_the_fire 
 to_link_the_fire : This ending is obtained by lighting the bonfire that appears after defeating Gwyn, Lord of Cinder. In sacrifice, the Chosen Undead links the First Flame as Gwyn had done before him/her, thus fulfilling Kingseeker Frampt's goal of continuing the Age of Fire. The Curse of the Undead will be broken, but one day the flames will fade again, and all will play out as before.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In Ending 2: "The End of Fire", the First Flame is snuffed out, albeit with the Fire Keeper revealing that one day "tiny flames will dance across the darkness", which suggests that the First Flame partially perseveres in the form of embers within the Lords of Cinder of the past. As these Lords will use these embers of the First Flame to exert influence the world, this Age of Dark does not spell finality for the Flame. Alternatively, the player can choose to intervene as the Fire Keeper is about to extinguish the First Flame, by killing her before the cinematic ends. In this ending, the Ashen One instead takes the First Flame for themselves while the final segment of the opening narration is heard: *"Nameless, accursed Undead, unfit even to be cinder...And so it is...that Ash seeketh embers."*

title: Chosen Undead
snippet: ***Dark Lord:** This ending is unlocked if the player leaves the arena after killing Lord Gwyn. title: Lords
snippet:
Fearing the upcoming Age of Dark and potentially humans as well, Gwyn took some of his knights with him left to the Kiln of the First Flame, sacrificing himself to rekindle the First Flame. The Black Knights who followed after Gwyn were reduced to ash, and Gwyn himself became hollow.

The extension of the Age of Fire was not without consequences. As a result, the undead curse arose from Gwyn's actions. Humans who were afflicted by the curse bore the Darksign. Those that bore it would be revived after death, though their humanity would be lost, and without restoring it would eventually lose their sanity.

snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - other_known_unkindled

In her first life, she was the leader of the Sable Church of Londor, which aims to end the Age of Fire and bring about the Age of Dark; as such, she might have aimed to seize the First Flame rather than to link it. In her second life, Elfriede, now renamed Friede, renounced her past, instead making a home in the Painted World of Ariandel.

snippet: Lothric, the younger prince, was the destined Lord of Cinder, who was tasked with sacrificing himself as fuel for the First Flame to uphold the Age of Fire. The prince, born a sickly, frail child, was nevertheless viewed as the "last hope of his line", the culmination of generations of Lothric rulers obsessed with producing worthy Champions for the Flame. snippet:
Flame God Flann -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Flann is one of the members of Gwyn's clan who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire. He was worshiped by the humans as the flame god.

After Lord Gwyn linked the First Flame and his firstborn son was dethroned and exiled, Flann abandoned Anor Londo together with nearly all of the other deities and moved to an unknown location in the world of men, which eventually led him to marry Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight. With her, he'd sire an unknown number of children of divine lineage, continuing the royal family's bloodline.

snippet:

 the_ringed_city : If the Ashen One follows Gael, they will find themselves in the Dreg Heap, an amalgamation of collapsed kingdoms and civilizations at the end of time. Within the Dreg Heap they may encounter Lapp, a hollow who seeks the Purging Monument in order to remember his past life. Fighting their way past the Dreg Heap they find two demons, the Demon in Pain & the Demon Below. Following the fall of the last of the two, its corpse is enkindled by the Chaos Flame and reawakened as the Demon Prince. Defeating the Demon Prince allows the Ashen One to travel to the Ringed City, the first city of Man, inhabited by the Pygmies. Gwyn, the first Lord of Cinder, had gifted the city to humanity after the end of the Age of Ancients, along with his daughter Filianore.

title: Londor
snippet: The three sisters shared Kaathe's aim of ending the Age of Fire founded by the gods and ushering the Age of Dark; however, the means and the ultimate goal differed from Kaathe's original vision. The sisters of Londor sought to crown not a "Lord of Men", but instead a "Lord of Hollows", who they claimed would wear "the true face of man". By the time of the Sable Church, the form of the Hollow appears to have been acknowledged as the original condition, the "most honest shape", of humans; whether this position was espoused by Kaathe himself is uncertain. Moreover, instead of leaving the First Flame to die out, the Sable Church wished for their Lord of Hollows to usurp the Flame, to "wrest it from its mantle", which would empower their new Lord. This mission seems to align with Vendrick's own wisdom, who viewed a true leader as one who would "inherit fire and harness the dark". title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
Toxic and poison work well on all three of them, allowing high damage to be dealt at relatively low risk.

When pursuing the player in melee, the bosses are willing to chase them over the arena's ledges into the water. They tend to hesitate at the edge before jumping, and when landing will pause for a moment even after they're no longer locked into the landing animation. Thus, goading the bosses into chasing you over these edges is a reliable way to get a safe, if small opening to hit them after they land, to get a slight lead over Varg and the Graverobber in their pursuit of you with which to get a hit in on Cerah, or to hit them with ranged attacks when they linger at the top of the ledge. Be careful not to stand directly below any of the bosses when doing this, as they can perform plunging attacks on you.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet: The AI pathing also seems to have a slight preference for taking the ramps down instead of jumping off the ledges, so if you jump off while the bosses aren't particularly close or, after dropping, wander too far from the edge closest to the bosses or too close to the ramp, they may opt to take the ramp instead. This pathing preference is not terribly strong, you do not need to wait until the last second to jump off or hug the wall after jumping, just don't drop when your pursuers are halfway across the room or start running for the ramp before they've followed you over the edge.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategies 
 strategies : Cerah the Old Explorer will shoot the player constantly if left alive while dealing with the other two, so it is helpful to either take him out first or move toward him in order to make him draw his Estoc. If left alone to shoot at the player, Cerah has incredibly high damage potential, as he is likely to stagger the player on top of doing high damage, indirectly increasing the damage output of both Varg or the Graverobber. Cerah is the most agile of the three, being able to consistently dodge many attacks, including backstabs. Attacking Cerah will cause his other two team members to charge at the attacker.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet: Another good strategy is to use the NPC summons Ruined Aflis and Rapacious Andrei to distract either Graverobber or Varg, preferably both, then repeatedly backstab them while they focus on the summons. They will likely turn their attention back to you afterward, but retreating or switching targets can cause them to focus on the summons again, allowing the strategy to be repeated. It is still important to watch for Cerah’s arrows while doing this. Once Graverobber and Varg are defeated, Cerah will be left alone, making the end of the fight much easier, especially if one or both summons are still alive. Or if preferred, focusing on Cerah after just one of his allies is killed in an attempt to eliminate the arrows. Again, the summons should keep the other distracted if you choose to do it this way.

 lead : The , , and are a trio of bosses in *Dark Souls II: Crown of the Sunken King*.

Found at the end of the Cave of the Dead, a location past the Priestess' Chamber bonfire in [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Shulva,_Sanctum_City Shulva], they are all fought at once and each have their own individual health bar.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
Ancient Solder Varg uses equipment associated with Havel the Rock: Havel's Set, the Dragon Tooth, and Havel's Greatshield.

Cerah the Old Explorer dons a mixture of sets, namely the Lucatiel's Mask headwear part of Lucatiel's Set, the Black Leather chest armor part of the Black Leather Set, and the Leather Gloves and Leather Boots part of the Hunter's Set. His main weapon is a Dragonslayer Greatbow, although he will switch to an Estoc thrusting sword if the player gets close; he only ever wields one of these two weapons, using both hands.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
All three are capable of backstabbing the player. This means caution should be taken while healing. They move slower than the player while in the water, which can be used as an advantage to get away from them, although this can become a disadvantage if Cerah's line-of-sight is not broken.

They are very susceptible to being "pancaked" by 2-handed great hammers, the only exception being Varg while he's attacking. With good positioning, you can even pancake Varg and the Graverobber together, and keep squashing them as they get up, as long as Cerah doesn't have line of sight to shoot you. This is probably the fastest way to end the fight.

Toxic and poison work well on all three of them, allowing high damage to be dealt at relatively low risk.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
The Afflicted Graverobber is a very powerful enemy, causing heavy bleed buildup and being able to catch the player in a stunlock. The damage potential she possesses is phenomenal. The Graverobber will work alongside Varg in a melee situation, stunning the player, then having Varg follow it up with a smash. This is best avoided by trying to separate them and taking them on one at a time.

Ancient Soldier Varg is by far the hardest to topple of the three enemies. Should he reach lower than half of his health, he will begin healing with an Estus Flask. He spends most of his time blocking with his greatshield, though, meaning there will be multiple opportunities to guard break him. He will attempt to work as a tank for his comrades, constantly trying to get in the way to take as much damage for them as he can.

 dark_souls_iii : In the time of Lothric, more Corvians are seen outside the painting, some of them even acting as storytellers who share tales of their frigid home. Their stories are considered heretical, and most of their listeners are Corvians themselves. All of them have no place to go, and seemingly yearn to return to the frozen landscape of their painting.

These aren't the only descendants of the Crow People, however, and many of them still exist within a new Painted World, restored by Father Ariandel. He appears to be a large humanoid akin to a Giant, but shows some crow-like features across his body, like fuzzy legs and talon-like hands. It's unclear if he was one of the Corvians, but he was one of the more important figures of their society. The most important one by far was the mistress of the Painted World, who wielded a great scythe, which became a symbol of a long-lost home to the forlorn corvids.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet:
Corvian (Lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : By the time of Drangleic, knowledge of the Painted World had been lost. Regardless, some of its Corvian inhabitants took their leave, as one of their descendants, Weaponsmith Ornifex, can be found in the old town of Tseldora. Her choice to live in Tseldora seems rather curious, as the town has some passing connection to the ancient Goddess of Sin. It's unclear if she even knows of her and how relevant she used to be to her people.

She uses a special forging technique that originated from a strange being that once inhabited the area, though she is unaware of what it truly was. She also believes humans to be inherently different than her kind, suggesting that across the ages, the Crow People had forgotten that they originated from humans. This was probably not helped by the general distrust humanity displays when dealing with creatures who are different than them.

 description : Corvians are transformed humans, warped by their obsessive devotion to Velka, Goddess of Sin. They are surprisingly varied in appearance, varying in how humanoid or bird-like they are. The earliest ones had lanky, androgynous bodies with crow heads, large wings replacing their arms, and red feet, while the later ones looked like emaciated humanoids with feathered legs and bird-like feet, capable of sprouting wings separate from their arms, though they lacked any real corvid feature in their faces. Lastly, most of the ones living in the painting, deprived of wings and sporting a few scattered feathers, but with an undeniable bird head with desaturated white eyes. Their knights are like a mix of this latter type and the very first one, showing a lanky yet imposing frame, while having no wings of their own. They are characterized as being unwanted, forlorn beings with no place to call home.

 dark_souls : The Corvians have humble beginnings. Once, they were simple human worshippers of the Goddess Velka, who transformed through their devotion. In the time of Lordran, they were best known as Crow People of Velka, or simply Crow Demons. Despite being called "demons", they share no relation with the Chaos Demons of Izalith, as they were ultimately human in nature.

At some point, these devotees would find themselves in the Painted World of Ariamis, either banished there or simply seeking an escape from the real world, along with many of Velka's artifacts and a peculiar crossbreed child. Whether they transformed before setting foot within the painting or afterwards is unclear, but their presence was entirely localized within the frigid landscape, with none of them found elsewhere in this age. They are hostile to all those who enter the painting and don't belong there.

 strategies : Gwyndolin's boss battle takes place in a seemingly never-ending corridor.

He is not a very difficult boss if the player has decent dodging skills. Of his three attacks, two can be avoided by hiding behind pillars, while the last one is more powerful and fast (he will tend to use the Sphere Shot after Orb Spread if the player is hiding behind pillars). The main issue in this fight is reaching him, as he will teleport away when the player approaches (equipping the Ring of Fog may increase the time available to attack before he teleports), meaning that the best time to run up to him is when he is just finishing off his Arrow Spread, as he takes a few moments to recover. snippet: It is possible to theorize that, although Gwyn's Firstborn had been disinherited, stripped of his deific stature and eradicated from history, Gwyndolin, as the new king of the gods, tried to get closer to his brother by recalling him to the new city created for the descendants of the gods. In fact, an altar without a statue in the center of the city of Irithyll contains the Ring of the Sun's First Born that he himself had left in front of his father's Mausoleum when he left Anor Londo, implying that Gwyndolin had prepared a place to welcome his older brother back into the pantheon of gods and allow again his worship if he ever returned.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: It is possible to theorize that the ritual combat of the "Battle of Stoicism" was created in Oolacile by Gwyndolin as a prototype of the more complicated Firelinking system that would later include the Bells of Awakening and Sen's Fortress. In fact, the victorious warriors were welcomed to Anor Londo, presumably to be tested again before obtaining the Lordvessel. It should be noted that Gwyn had entrusted her sons to continue the path of Firelink and guide the humans to maintain the Age of Fire.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Both the Orb and Arrow Spread attacks are avoidable by hiding behind one of the pillars on either side of the corridor. The Sphere Shot, on the other hand, will go through walls, inflicting full damage if not blocked or avoided. The Orb Spread and Sphere Shot are Magic-based, though, so a shield that can block 100% physical damage and has good Magic resistance, like the Crest Shield, is recommended for this fight.

While devastating, both the Sphere Shot and Arrow Spread attacks have no tracking whatsoever and are easily avoided simply by running diagonally. If a player does not want to risk it too much, a good strategy to catch up to him is by moving from pillar to pillar until they are about two pillars away from Gwyndolin and then wait until he shoots his Arrow Spread. This attack can consist of two-to-four arrow barrages. Wait until he finishes the second one and go for him, if he shoots any subsequent arrows, dodge them by running diagonally.

 theories : It is possible to theorize that Gwyndolin is the result of the union of Gwyn and Crossbreed Priscilla for several reasons:
**Gwyndolin is the last child of Gwyn; but Yorshka, a half-dragon, is his younger sister, confirming that they share a mother. Since the two siblings both possess draconic traits, their common mother should have possessed draconic traits herself for them to inherit them partially.
**Gwyndolin, despite being another children of Gwyn, did not inherit the power of Sunlight like the rest of his father's lineage. Instead he inherited the magic of the moon that made him a powerful moon sorcerer, a power that was unique to the white dragon Seath, the probable father of Priscilla.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: The first demon who manifested itself was the youngest son of Izalith. He was a younger brother of the other witches who gifted him a magic ring to negate his pain from the lava sores that tortured him. However, the still-unstable Flame of Chaos led him to transform into a monstrous demon and drop his ring, leaving the flames of chaos to burn him constantly as he couldn't control them, while also generating another distorted Centipede Demon. Despite becoming the first distorted creature created by the Flame of Chaos, at a certain point Izalith and her daughters managed to stabilize the new power they had created and began to generate the first real demons: life forms with stable bodies and capable of controlling the flame of chaos within each of them. title: Demon (lore)
snippet: The sorcerers of Oolacile, capable of manipulating the forces of nature with knowledge and means that not even the sorcerers of Vinheim were able to replicate, created the Sanctuary Guardians, an amalgamation of traits from several animals like lions, goats, scorpions and birds, to defend the Sanctuary Garden of their country. Although these creatures were not created by the Bed of Chaos and therefore cannot be defined as "demons", the process with which they were obtained, mixing characteristics of different animals thanks to the sorcery of souls and life, makes them very similar to the demons of chaos, produced by a flame created in imitation of the First Flame.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: Although the lower half of their bodies were transformed into a chaos spider, Quelaag and her sister managed to carve out a domain for themselves on the edge of the realm of Izalith, near what was called Blighttown. While the older Quelaag maintained control over their refuge thanks to her strength, the younger one, who was a Fire Keeper with an immense amount of humanity within her, began producing eggs by the dozen, until they covered their entire lair. In time, the Undead exiled to the depths of the Undead Burg and who had ended up in the rotten Blighttown chose to serve the Flame of Chaos and the two demonic daughters of Izalith of their own free will.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: Alsanna, as the heiress to her Lord's wishes and in reverence of the apocalypse, devoted herself and the power of her Dark Soul to a ritual in the hopes of appeasing the raging flame. With the ivory gates opened, the land of Eleum Loyce grew cold and lifeless, turning into a frigid expanse, in an attempt to freeze Chaos along with the entire country. The remaining Knights of Eleum Loyce remained to watch over the Garrison Ward under the King's final orders to contain the Chaos, waiting patiently for a new leader strong enough to guide them into its depths, while Alsanna remained in prayer inside the Cathedral over the depths to continue the ritual. The Old Chaos was thus contained, albeit it corrupted the Ivory King and his knights, nevertheless remaining confined by Alsanna's tireless effort. Chaos was repressed until a Bearer of the Curse came along and destroyed the Burnt King and his corrupted Eleum Loyce knights, definitively eradicating the offshoots of Chaos from Drangleic.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: Like humanity and the Gods of Anor Londo of old, the demons seek to rekindle the Flame of Chaos to preserve their race. A Demon Prince, a champion of their race, challenged Prince Lorian of Lothric, only to be defeated and retreat without his memory of the flames. No longer able to pursue the rekindling of the Chaos Flame, the demon race was condemned to extinction; as time went on, even the few remaining demons all but lacked any trace of the flame within; one such lost demon, reduced to little more than a wood and stone golem, served as a gatekeeper of Lothric.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: By the time of the awakening of the Ashen One, the Flame of Chaos had begun to fail, making the ancient Demons a dying race. The ruins of Izalith are littered with huge piles of corpses of ancient Demons, most of them belonging to lesser Capra Demons and Taurus Demons, while few surviving specimens aimlessly roam a world that has no place for them. These beings, called Stray Demons, look like their ancestors only superficially since their body is smaller and made mostly by rock, wood and lava (much like the Bed of Chaos). They have decayed and petrified to the point of being able to spew mere boulders, instead of flames. The Batwing Demons, a lesser breed of ancient Demons, were unfazed by the Chaos Flame's extinction and kept their duty as "ferrymen" for those who followed the legacy of Gwyn (thus proving a deep connection between their kin and the Gods).

title: Demon (lore)
snippet:
Beings twisted by Chaos into something else, like the Bed of Chaos or the Burnt Ivory King (as the Flame of Chaos would survive past the Bed of Chaos' death) are not categorized as Chaos Demons, as the term applies only to beings conceived by the Bed itself. The Bed's eventual demise in *Dark Souls* means that Demons, who cannot reproduce, now exist in a finite number, and by the time of *Dark Souls III* they are a dying race, close to extinction. Besides Chaos Demons are cretures also called 'demons' despite being fundamentally different in their origins, likely due to individuals being unaware of the distinctions.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: As a symbol of their dedication they became Egg Burdened, welcoming the parasitic eggs produced by Quelaag's sister into their bodies. In this way the eggs would hatch inside them, first producing Vile Maggots which would then develop into Giant Mosquitoes and ultimately into smaller insectoid demons: the Cragspiders. Quelaag's plan, with the help of her sister, was therefore to reproduce in miniature a version of the Bed of Chaos that would use humanity as fertilizer for eggs and the undead as hosts to create new, albeit lesser, demons. To receive help in their goal they even created the covenant of the Chaos Servants, which would welcome servants of the Daughter of Chaos with the aim of accumulating humanity by killing other Undead which they would then give to Quelaag's sister and in exchange get the chance to learn their pyromancies and a shortcut to their hometown of Lost Izalith.

 lead : **Demons** are a race in the *Dark Souls* universe.

"True" Demons (labelled **Chaos Demons** in this article), are beings (some unique, others members of specific sub-species) originating from the fall of Izalith prior to *Dark Souls*, during which the Witch of Izalith lost control of her Lord Soul, causing the creation of the Flame of Chaos that twisted beings in Izalith and turned the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, a creative force that kept on endlessly making new lifeforms: Demons, which spilled from Izalith into the world. They typically have affinities for fire and/or stone.
